articles.title: Christian metal band sues Netflix over KPop Demon Hunters name
articles.summary: 25-year-old band Demon Hunter says name of streamer’s hit movie creates ‘substantial confusion’ among consumers. Christian metal band Demon Hunter is suing Netflix, accusing the entertainment giant of trademark infringement and unfair competition tied to the blockbuster “KPop Demon Hunters” name.
body: The lawsuit was filed Tuesday by Hyde Lane, the company behind Demon Hunter, and alleges that Netflix Studios and concert promoter AEG Presents have created “substantial confusion” among consumers.

“Demon Hunter [is] a well-known and celebrated metal band. Demon Hunter was formed at the turn of the century and, in the quarter-century since, it has consistently released albums, toured, and sold merchandise to a large and dedicated audience,” the Tuesday filing stated, according to the Wrap.

“Unfortunately, in 2025, Netflix and Netflix Studios – despite almost certainly being aware of Demon Hunter – chose to release a movie titled ‘KPop Demon Hunters’,” the filing said, adding that the film “reached unprecedented levels of success, not only as a film on Netflix’s streaming service, but also via the ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ movie soundtrack album and merchandise”.
The band, who have been releasing music and touring for 25 years, says the alleged confusion has already had real-world consequences.
points: 25-year-old band Demon Hunter says name of streamer’s hit movie creates ‘substantial confusion’ among consumers.

articles.title: Tom Holland set to earn $100m from Spider-Man: Brand New Day
articles.summary: In a year that’s seen the British actor star in the season’s two biggest blockbusters – and marry his co-star from both – he is reportedly earning a huge pay packet thanks to box-office bonuses.
body: The British actor Tom Holland is expected to “make at least $100m” for starring in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, according to the Wrap.

Unnamed sources “with knowledge of Holland’s deal” say he was paid $20m (£15m) upfront, about double what he reportedly received for his previous Spider-Man film No Way Home in 2021. But the extraordinary success of Brand New Day at the global box office means the 30-year-old is expected to earn another $80m or more in backend bonuses.

Holland’s reported salary represents a vast increase from his previous performances in the role. When he first played Spider-Man, in a relatively brief but significant appearance in Captain America: Civil War (2016), he was reportedly paid $250,000. For the next three Spider-Man films in which he starred, Homecoming (2017), Far from Home (2019), and No Way Home, he was reportedly paid $500,000, $4m and $10m respectively. But his initial contract is thought to have expired after the end of No Way Home, and the hugely increased remuneration is the result of a freshly negotiated new deal.

articles.title: Coyote Vs Acme review – quirky comedy returns from the dead to flip Wile E Coyote’s slapstick-violent world
articles.summary: After being shelved as a tax-writeoff, this Looney Tunes reboot redraws the hapless hunter as the Erin Brockovich of the cartoon world. Here is a quirky, peculiar, yet strangely diverting live-action-toon hybrid of the kind that hasn’t been popular at the movies for many a day; it gives us a new…
body: Coyote Vs Acme is a comedy whose obsessive and hyperactive pedantry is exhausting, but arguably part of the point, aimed at America’s litigious culture, corporate arrogance and monopoly capitalism. So when producers Warner Bros initially decided to shelve the whole thing as a tax writeoff, that must have felt to director Dave Green like an ironic cartoon anvil to the head. Well, the film was rescued and it would be great therefore to discover that this is a masterpiece. Sadly it’s not, but there are some laughs and the pure fanatical oddity makes this watchable.

articles.title: ‘Insidious: Out of the Further’ Review: Latest Entry in the Franchise Serves Up Genuinely Terrifying Setpieces Despite a Convoluted Final Act
articles.summary: If you’ve always been terrified of dental work and the idea of someone poking around your pearly whites with sharp tools, you’re not alone. With “Insidious: Out of the Further,” the sixth entry in the infinitely inventive horror franchise, writer-director Jacob Chase is unashamed to declare that he…
body: Director Jacob Chase nails the polished horror series’ creepy vibes and an inventive dream world that could have benefited from a leaner story.

The patient in question is one of a trio of dead people strolling around Gemma’s neighborhood; another is styled in such a hagsploitation manner that it’s impossible not to think of Aunt Gladys from “Weapons.” The entities continually lurk into Gemma’s house and into the eyes of her precocious nine-year-old daughter, Maya (Island Austin), trying to intimidate the family of two. It’s actually curious that Gemma chose to stay in that same house after the events of the terrific opening prologue, set in 1999, in which the young Gemma (Charli Penton, brilliant in a short role) witnesses the brutal death of her fragile mother through an inexplicable series of supernatural happenings.

articles.title: ‘Building the Band’ Group Soulidified Signs to Atlantic Records (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Soulidified has signed to Atlantic Records, just a year after they were introduced to the world on Netflix’s “Building the Band,” Variety can exclusively announce. The group, consisting of Shade Jenifer, Malik Heard, Bradley Rittmann and Landon Boyce, was initially formed on “Building the Band,”…
body: Soulidified has been steadily grinding since their time on “Building the Band,” releasing their debut original single “One & Only” in August 2025 and their latest “What’s Your Name” this past February. The group recently supported Khalid on four of his shows and are currently plotting their “What’s Your Name” tour, which will touch down in Brazil, Amsterdam, Paris, Berlin and London this fall.

“From the first time I saw them on ‘Building the Band,’ I knew these four had a rare quality I hadn’t seen in any group I’ve managed before,” says Soulidified’s manager Johnny Wright, an industry veteran who has steered the careers of Backstreet Boys and New Kids on the Block. Wright manages the group alongside Day to Day Management’s Fernando Watson and Jayvon Hicks. “Beyond their obvious vocal and performance talent,” continues Wright, “the fact that they came together sight unseen makes it clear God had a hand in their story. I’m proud to be part of their journey and especially excited that they are now a part of the Bee/Wright Entertainment, Atlantic Records, and WME family.”

articles.title: Netflix Buys Wu-Tang Clan Doc ‘The Disciple’ Directed by Joanna Natasegara (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable” the Sundance-bowing doc that unravelled the story of Dutch-Moroccan rapper and producer Cilvaringz and the making of the controversial Wu-Tang Clan record “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” is heading to Netflix.
body: But the film also charts how Cilvaringz’ “ambition and creativity” would converge to see him record “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” a 31-track record of which only copy was made and in 2015 was auctioned off to the highest bidder. “It’s scarcity is a form of protest, and an argument that music still holds intrinsic worth as art in a digital age,” reads the synopsis. “The result is one of the most controversial artifacts of our time that sparked ongoing conversations about technology, creation and ownership.”

Unfortunately, the record’s highest bidder — who paid $2 million, making it the most expensive musical work ever sold — was notorious (and later convicted) entrepreneur Martin Shkreli, adding further controversy over the project.

articles.title: Nielsen Makes New Bid to Capture ‘Co-Viewing’ as TV Season Approaches
articles.summary: Nielsen is really working the room. The media-measurement giant aims to measure viewers of video content more accurately and will place a focus on capturing so-called “co-viewing,” or multiple viewers watching the same piece of programming together at the same location.
body: “We are relentless in our pursuit of delivering the most accurate measurement possible for our media and advertising clients,” said Karthik Rao, CEO of Nielsen, in a statement. “We’ve spent months working hand in hand with them and industry experts to make Big Data + Panel even more accurate.”

Despite the rise of a swath of new competitors, Nielsen’s measurement remains the bedrock element of determining the size and other attributes of video audiences, and is a key element in data that helps underpin value and price in talks between advertisers and TV networks and streamers. Nielsen launched a “Big Data + Panel” product in early 2025 that could examine audience interactions with cable and satellite set-top boxes and smart TVs across 45 million households and 75 million devices.

The company has faced some backlash, with the Video Advertising Bureau, an advocacy group that represents major video publishers and TV networks to the advertising industry, accusing Nielsen of releasing data that could be inconsistent.

articles.title: Over/Under review – beautiful coming of age story of female best friends set across five summers
articles.summary: There’s an astonishing naturalism about the two leads, navigating the ups and downs of adolescence, bodily changes and learning to use tampons. Practically any woman who had a best female friend in early adolescence will be able to relate to this fragile, thoughtful drama about two American…
body: As the film starts, the two are nine-year-old besties, spending their summers together in New England where they go to camp, frolic in the surf (the title refers to a game they play with waves) and try to sleep over at each other’s houses. Unfortunately, Stella can’t yet cope with sleeping through the night at someone else’s place, and every time they try she must be collected by her parents after waking up frightened in the night. But it’s still something the girls yearn for. They even wish for it when they trap morning moths in jars, hoping fairies will grant them their hearts’ desires.

articles.title: Angélique Kidjo makes history for Africa with star on Hollywood Walk of Fame
articles.summary: Without Africans, no music is possible on this planet, says the 66-year-old musical icon from Benin.
body: Five-time Grammy award winner Angélique Kidjo has made history as the first African musician to get a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

"We Africans just don't know what we've given to the world, and what we continue giving to the world for the music to exist. Without us, there's no music possible on this planet," the musical icon, who comes from Benin, said at the ceremony.
She was joined by her family, friends and stars such as Hollywood actors Willem Dafoe and Djimon Hounsou, who is also from Benin, and Nigerian musician Adekunle Gold.
For more than four decades, Kidjo, 66, has taken African sounds to global audiences, blending influences from her native Benin with funk, jazz and pop.

articles.title: Emma Barnett reveals she 'had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have'
articles.summary: The BBC Radio 4 Today programme presenter explained her recent absence on her return on Wednesday.
body: BBC presenter Emma Barnett has revealed she had a hysterectomy and surgery for endometriosis days before a documentary she made about the condition was broadcast.
Barnett, 41, returned to Radio 4's Today programme on Wednesday morning, explaining she had been absent in recent weeks because she was in hospital "in a case of life imitating work".
She told listeners: "I made a programme on endometriosis on BBC Two and ended up being in hospital for endometriosis.
"So yes, I've been recuperating, shall we say, from surgery for endometriosis and a hysterectomy to boot. So that's been less fun than the Today programme, but it is lovely to be back."

articles.title: Nielsen Rolls Out Suite of TV Ratings Updates for 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The ratings provider says the changes in co-viewing measurement, TV universe estimates and other areas will bring more accurate data to clients.
body: Nielsen will incorporate a slate of updates and “enhancements” to its TV ratings product for the 2026-27 season, including a change to its monthly snapshot of viewing across various platforms that sparked a small controversy earlier this year.

That change — a different way of measuring the total number of TV users in the United States — along with updates to co-viewing measurement, more accurate weighting of the big data and panel components in TV ratings and other tweaks are set to be incorporated into Nielsen’s product starting Sept. 1, after passing muster with oversight body the Media Rating Council. Data for clients and publicly released numbers aren’t likely to change significantly, but Nielsen is touting a product that will be more accurate.
